evidence.verification: PASS: one durable Q1 consumer group with volatile leased delivery, durable CONSUMER_ACK/CURSOR_CHECKPOINT records, generation fencing and contiguous sparse cursor recovery, exercised by real external SDK consumer processes over TCP.
evidence.observed_result: 188 workspace tests pass:19 protocol WAL-independent frames plus2 new FETCH_END vectors (21 protocol),31 WAL,49 default durable (14 group actor),12 server,19 SDK,13 transport.51 fault-enabled durable tests.8 standalone replay,6 durable-consumer and20 TCP/process fault fixtures pass. Q0/Q1 process smokes, documentation and formatting pass.
evidence.wire_contract: Existing FETCH(17)/MESSAGE(12)/CONSUMER_ACK(13)/CONSUMER_ACK_RESULT(14) and all field IDs preserved. Additive terminal FETCH_END=26 (has_more field50 reused) after zero or more MESSAGE frames. FETCH with absent/zero group_generation claims and durably fences a generation; nonzero must match or STALE_GENERATION(18). MESSAGE carries the full token including ownership_epoch and delivery_attempt; ACK validates every token field and returns ACK_COMMITTED only after the sync. CONSUMER_NACK/EXTEND_LEASE remain UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY. Golden B-04 and original big-endian vectors unchanged; new fetch-v1 vector is byte-exact.
evidence.wal_compatibility: v1 record/segment/manifest layouts unchanged. Reuses reserved kinds CONSUMER_ACK=3 (RQCA v1 payload: group,generation,owner epoch,lease,offset,attempt,principal,message) and CURSOR_CHECKPOINT=5 (RQCP v1: group,generation,cursor,ascending sparse offsets). Recovery is kind-aware: MESSAGE must be immediately followed by its PRODUCER_OUTCOME; orphan outcomes, malformed ACK/checkpoint payloads, ACKs for unknown messages, checkpoints ahead of their append and decreasing generations fail closed. Existing publication-only storage recovers without migration. Application offsets stay stable but become sparse; standalone replay skips metadata records and returns the next unread WAL position as continuation.
evidence.cursor_semantics: ACK of C alone, then B, must not advance the cursor past A; ACK of A advances through the previously acknowledged B/C. The sparse set is bounded (4096 default) and the gap-closing cursor offset is always accepted. Checkpoints embed the cursor and full sparse set, so compaction cannot erase acknowledged gaps. Restart reconstructs gaps and the contiguous prefix; unacknowledged records are redelivered with a fresh lease. Only application MESSAGE offsets participate; producer outcomes/ACKs/checkpoints never create cursor gaps and next offsets are never derived by incrementing.
evidence.crash_recovery: Process fixtures kill the broker at BeforeAppend, AfterAppendBeforeSync and AfterSyncBeforeReply of a CONSUMER_ACK. Before append and before sync redeliver the record and never report ACK_COMMITTED; after sync the cursor is recovered at the end and the acknowledged record is not redelivered. A parent-owned JSON journal records delivery token, message identity, payload hash, generation, lease and received ACK_COMMITTED. SIGKILL after an externally observed ACK preserves the cursor. Clean shutdown with an outstanding lease keeps the committed ACK and redelivers only the unacknowledged record.
evidence.sdk_semantics: Client::fetch_q1_group validates every MESSAGE scope/group/generation/lease/attempt, strictly increasing offsets and count/byte bounds before accepting mandatory FETCH_END. Client::ack_q1_group never mints or retries tokens and returns ACK_COMMITTED only after validated correlation and identity. Transport loss/timeout before the terminal frame returns Incomplete and closes the stream; a partial batch is never success. Duplicate tokens resolve to the saved committed result. GroupOptions generation None claims/replaces; Some continues and surfaces StaleGeneration.
evidence.resource_and_authority: AUTH principal1 plus configured tenant/topic/partition/incarnation authorize group fetch and ACK. Actor admission reserves WAL scratch, batch bytes and retained responses against the partition budget before IO; 14 actor tests cover claim, ordered/sparse ACKs, duplicate lookup, fencing, expiry, invalid identity, corruption, concurrent identical ACKs, admission and cancellation. Bounds: 8 groups, 256 leases, 4096 sparse entries, 4MiB leased bytes, 30s lease, checkpoint every 64 ACKs. Lease grants are volatile; group generation, ACK and cursor are durable.
evidence.limitations: Single-node local Q1 only; one active mutation generation per group but no competing-worker rebalance, NACK, retry schedule, DLQ/quarantine, SEEK or cursor export. Lease tokens and delivery attempts are process-scoped and reset after restart. The authenticated principal/tenant model is the existing trusted loopback static identity, not production TLS/ACL. CHECKPOINT compaction retains the sparse set but not old ACK-record history. An irrecoverably lost Q1 history still requires explicit authorized reinitialization with a fresh incarnation; recovery never resets progress. No physical power-loss certification and no exactly-once application-processing claim.
evidence.next_note: B-07 is the next correctness gate (external acknowledged set versus recovered WAL under repeated SIGKILL); B-06 remains the terminal-disposition (NACK/retry/quarantine/DLQ) work package.

followup.verification: PASS: a previously committed ACK token remains resolvable as a saved read-only outcome after a generation fence, appending no new durable record; the same fenced generation still cannot acknowledge a different unacknowledged record.
followup.observed_result: 15 durable group actor tests pass (50 default durable tests, 189 workspace tests when the full suite is run).

tasks.title: DLQ and quarantine
tasks.proof: Crash between DLQ commit and source terminal record leaves no cursor skip and no duplicate DLQ message

evidence.verification: PASS: real external consumers NACK Q1 deliveries; bounded retry, quarantine, durable terminal disposition and a real replayable Q1 DLQ were exercised over TCP with independent journals and six deliberate broker kills across the PENDING/DLQ/terminal ordering.
evidence.observed_result: 200 workspace tests, 24 protocol, 31 WAL, 57 default durable (7 terminal), 59 fault-enabled durable, 16 testkit, 13 server and 19 SDK tests pass. 28 oracle self-corruption, 12 NACK/terminal, 9 B-07 durability, 8 replay, 6 consumer and 20 process-fault fixtures pass. Q0/Q1 smokes, documentation and formatting pass.
evidence.wire_contract: Additive CONSUMER_NACK_RESULT=27 with field NACK_OUTCOME=51; existing CONSUMER_NACK fields and all prior IDs/encodings unchanged. Outcomes are RETRY_SCHEDULED(1, retry_after_ms), RETRY_EXHAUSTED(2), TERMINAL_COMMITTED(3), TERMINAL_PENDING(4) and ALREADY_CLOSED(5), each with disposition identity where applicable. ACK_COMMITTED is never reused for NACK acceptance. Golden vector nack-v1 pins the frame; negative tests reject outcome 0, missing retry delay and missing disposition.
evidence.retry_semantics: NACK validates principal, tenant/group/topic/partition, incarnation, offset, ownership epoch, generation, lease and attempt. It never acknowledges processing or advances the cursor. Backoff is initial delay doubled per attempt, capped by retry_max; max_attempts is configurable. Repeated NACK of the same attempt is idempotent. Lease expiry/disconnect make a record eligible for redelivery; generation replacement fences old leases. Retry/attempt state is durable in RETRY(7) records. Exhaustion without a terminal policy persists and leaves the message incomplete.
evidence.terminal_semantics: Terminal disposition is PENDING then COMMITTED in the same Q1 WAL using TERMINAL_DISPOSITION(4) with an RQTD v1 payload. Only a committed disposition enters the sparse completed set and may advance the contiguous cursor. Quarantine keeps the source publication and closes only its offset. Disposition IDs are deterministic from group/incarnation/offset. Corrupt or inconsistent committed terminal metadata fails recovery closed.
evidence.dlq_ordering: The DLQ is a separate explicitly configured local Q1 partition with its own directory, incarnation, WAL and manifest. Ordering is PENDING source record, DLQ Q1 publication with stable disposition identity, verified destination commit, COMMITTED source record, cursor closure. The DLQ payload is RQDL v1 preserving original bytes and message identity and is readable via READ_FETCH. Publication is idempotent per disposition; a duplicate terminal token returns ALREADY_CLOSED without another DLQ message. DLQ unavailability reports DLQ_UNAVAILABLE and leaves the cursor unchanged.
evidence.crash_recovery: Six deliberate kills cover PENDING append/before sync, PENDING after sync, DLQ committed/before source terminal, committed terminal append/before sync, committed terminal after sync/before reply, and quarantine pending/before sync. Recovery reconciles durable PENDING records, republishes or verifies the DLQ message, completes the source terminal only after its own barrier, and re-verifies committed DLQ proofs at startup. Every crash window converged with exactly one DLQ record, retained source data, no duplicate publication and no cursor skip; before-fsync quarantine left the source incomplete and redeliverable.
evidence.oracle: q1_oracle.reconcile_terminal rejects terminal DLQ without prior publication, missing/duplicate destination, payload digest mismatch, terminal for an uncommitted source offset, unexplained cursor movement, stale-generation mutation and incomplete journals. 8 new corruption fixtures plus the existing 20 pass.
evidence.defect: Fixed a real regression: standalone replay skipped ACK/checkpoint metadata but not RETRY/TERMINAL_DISPOSITION, so replay after terminal disposition poisoned the actor and returned STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE. The skip set now includes all internal metadata; the TCP test asserts source replay after terminal closure.
evidence.limitations: Single-node local Q1 source and one local DLQ partition; no distributed atomic transaction, Q2/Raft, rebalance, retention or admin redrive. SIGKILL on intact ext4 is process-crash recovery, not physical power loss. Retry eligibility is not wall-clock preserved across restart (pending retries become immediately eligible), and attempts for crashes before a retry record may be replayed; this can cause more retries, never premature closure. EXTEND_LEASE and SEEK remain unsupported. At-least-once delivery is verified, not exactly-once execution.
evidence.next_note: B-06 completes Q1 terminal disposition. The next roadmap work is C-01 (inter-node routing/snapshots), followed by C-02/C-03; Q2 remains unimplemented.

tasks.title: Q1 oracle gate
tasks.proof: Externally acknowledged publication and consumer-ACK sets exactly reconciled with recovered Q1 history after repeated process crashes

evidence.verification: PASS: independent parent-owned fsynced journals reconciled exact publication identities/digests/incarnations/offsets and consumer ACK/cursor state against post-recovery reads through external TCP SDK clients after deliberate process termination.
evidence.observed_result: 190 workspace tests, 22 protocol, 31 WAL, 50 default durable, 52 fault-enabled durable, 16 testkit, 12 server, 19 SDK and 13 transport tests pass. 20 oracle self-corruption tests, 8 standalone replay, 6 durable-consumer, 20 TCP/process-fault and 9 B-07 campaign tests pass; Q0/Q1 process smokes and documentation pass.
evidence.crash_matrix: 26 oracle campaigns, all PASS, including 22 direct process terminations/fault injections: 6 publication kills (before append, after append/before sync, after sync/before reply; seeds 42/43), 8 consumer kills (same barriers plus cursor-checkpoint append/sync; seeds 44/45), 1 generation-claim kill before fence sync and 7 WAL fault points (append, partial-append, segment-sync, manifest-write/sync/rename, directory-sync) across a forced 512-byte segment rotation. Additional campaigns cover sparse out-of-order ACKs, generation replacement, corrupt/missing storage, Q0 isolation and measurements.
evidence.publication_reconciliation: Every externally received COMMITTED_LOCAL was recovered with the same message ID, SHA-256 payload digest, incarnation and offset. Before-append/before-sync crashes recovered 3/3 acknowledged records with one uncertain attempt absent; after-sync crash recovered 4/4 records with one explicitly uncertain, unacknowledged publication. Repeated committed tokens returned their original offsets; conflicting content was SequenceConflict; a new epoch starting at sequence 0 superseded an old epoch which was then ProducerFenced.
evidence.consumer_reconciliation: ACK before append/before sync stayed non-durable: the record was redelivered and the cursor remained at the incomplete offset. ACK after sync and ACK whose checkpoint append was killed before sync recovered cursor 4, did not redeliver the acknowledged record, and classified one lost-reply offset as uncertain committed progress. Sparse ACK of offset 2 left cursor 0 after restart and redelivered offsets 0 and 4; closing the gap advanced to end. No cursor crossed an unattempted or unacknowledged application record. Duplicate committed tokens resolved read-only after fencing; stale generations could not mutate; repeated restarts preserved identities and offsets.
evidence.oracle_reliability: Journals are append-only JSONL with per-record fsync outside broker storage and contiguous sequence numbers. PASS, FAIL, INVALID and NOT_RUN are distinct. 20 fixtures deliberately corrupt evidence (missing acknowledged record, changed digest, duplicate publication, wrong offset/incarnation, missing ACK state, cursor gap, stale-generation commit, truncated line, missing conclusion, sequence gap, unexplained recovered record) and all are rejected.
evidence.defect: Fixed a real sparse-offset codec defect: B-05 made application offsets sparse but major-1 validation still required even READ_RECORD/READ_END offsets, so replay after interleaved ACK/checkpoint records returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The codec now accepts in-range sparse positions; golden vectors are unchanged; regression tests added in crates/protocol/tests/read_replay.rs and the consumer crash matrix. Evidence and reproduction: benchmarks/evidence/q1-durability-5c4f92d/DEFECT.md.
evidence.measurements: Exploratory single-host n=200 debug-build observations: end-to-end COMMITTED_LOCAL p50 790us / p99 1.28ms; ACK_COMMITTED p50 720us / p99 1.15ms; direct WAL fsync p50 66us / p99 125us; append+fsync p50 148us / p99 249us; broker peak RSS 5804KiB; recovery readiness median 4.1ms (range 3.8-9.3ms); 200 recovered records. Q1 queue, producer/outcome, group/lease and sparse-set occupancy are UNAVAILABLE (no Q1 metric endpoint). p99.9 with n=200 is unstable. Not an SLO or power-loss claim.
evidence.limitations: SIGKILL on an intact ext4 filesystem is process-crash recovery, not physical power-loss or torn-write certification. One host, one Q1 partition, debug builds, no soak or cross-machine clocks. Single-consumer generation model only; no rebalance, NACK/retry schedule, DLQ/quarantine or SEEK (B-06 remains TODO). At-least-once delivery is verified; exactly-once application execution is not claimed. Small exploratory samples and UNAVAILABLE Q1 internal occupancy are reported honestly.
evidence.next_note: B-06 (Q1 terminal disposition: NACK/retry/quarantine/DLQ) is the next implementation package; C-05 depends on it.

tasks.title: Inter-node routing and snapshots
tasks.proof: Real two-process inter-node routing with validated identities, immutable snapshots, one-hop forwarding and loop avoidance

evidence.verification: PASS: two locally running brokers with distinct node IDs, cluster identity, peer ports, metadata fixtures and data directories exchange typed inter-node RPCs over real loopback TCP; a publication sent to the non-owner is forwarded exactly once and committed by the owner, returning the owner's own durable offset.
evidence.observed_result: Workspace tests pass with the new rovqet-control crate (24 control tests: 11 unit plus 13 real-socket integration tests). The Q0/Q1 process smokes, standalone replay, consumer, terminal/DLQ and B-07 durability suites remain green. Two multi-process cluster routing fixtures pass.
evidence.wire_contract: Separate inter-node namespace with an explicit portable binary envelope (magic RQCL, api_version, rpc_kind, flags, cluster_id u128, source_node u64, target_node u64, request_id u128, metadata_revision u64, ownership_epoch u64, timeout_budget_ms u32, body_len u32, bounded body, CRC32C). Normative RPC kind numbering is used verbatim (1 ROUTE_PUBLISH, 2 ROUTE_FETCH, 3 ROUTE_CONSUMER_ACK, 4 ROUTE_Q0_FANOUT, 5 METADATA_SNAPSHOT_GET, 6 OWNERSHIP_INSPECT, 7-9 Q1_TRANSFER_*, 10 HEALTH). Unknown kinds and unsupported versions are rejected; kinds 4 and 7-9 answer UNSUPPORTED. Client-facing frames and golden vectors are unchanged.
evidence.identities_and_trust: ClusterId, NodeId, PeerEndpoint, MetadataRevision, PartitionRef, partition owner, OwnershipEpoch, LeaseValidity, RpcRequestId, RpcKind and TimeoutBudget are distinct typed values; zero is reserved. The receiver validates cluster identity, target node and source against the configured static peer set, so a peer cannot assert ownership by supplying an epoch. The peer listener is loopback-only and refuses public binding.
evidence.metadata_snapshots: MetadataSnapshot carries cluster identity, revision, issued/revalidate bounds, node endpoints, topic policies, placements (owner, ownership epoch, lease validity, desired replicas, shard id) and acl/policy/capability revisions. Installation is atomic and validated (wrong cluster, revision regression, duplicate node or partition, unknown owner, zero epoch, missing lease, incompatible policy are rejected). A stale snapshot can never replace a newer one. A fresh process starts with no authority, so a restart cannot extend ownership; expired authority fails closed.
evidence.routing: One snapshot read per decision: local owner serves locally, a remote owner is forwarded exactly once, a stale epoch, expired authority, missing metadata or unknown partition return typed errors. A routed request is never routed again, which bounds redirect loops, and inconsistent maps between two nodes therefore cannot produce a ping-pong. The destination revalidates the routing authority before any mutation.
evidence.durable_semantics: Forwarded publication keeps the original producer token, epoch, sequence, message id, digest and QoS; the proxy never substitutes a token, mints an epoch or downgrades the class. Only the owner's local barrier produces COMMITTED_LOCAL, and the owner's durable outcome is returned unchanged. A timeout after the request was sent stays uncertain (client sees OUTCOME_UNKNOWN), never a definite rollback. The producer token stays authoritative at the owner: a retry returns the original offset without a second record.
evidence.bounds: 1 MiB maximum body, 64 outstanding peer requests, 64 concurrent peer connections, 2 s connect timeout, 5 s request timeout, 60 s maximum advertised timeout budget; all validated before allocation. Bounded connections, bounded pending requests and bounded concurrency are covered by tests.
evidence.limitations: Static development authority fixture, not a Raft-committed snapshot: no metadata consensus, membership management, placement rebalancing, coordinated handover, WAL migration, Q2 replication or majority acknowledgment. Consumer ROUTE_FETCH/ROUTE_CONSUMER_ACK are implemented at the owner but client-facing consumer traffic is not forwarded across nodes in C-01. Plaintext loopback peers with static identities are not production authentication. No cluster-scale benchmark or soak was run.
evidence.next_note: C-02 (metadata group, Raft-committed topology, epoch and lease renewal, staged Q1 transfer) is the next package; C-03 (Q2 storage adapter) depends on it.

tasks.title: Metadata group and fenced ownership
tasks.proof: Ownership fencing at the durable commit boundary is verified, the metadata Raft group commits and publishes the authoritative metadata, and a Q1 ownership handover is committed through the metadata group with a durable old-owner fence and a crash-safe promotion of the transferred history onto the successor

evidence.verification: PARTIAL: the metadata Raft group, the committed migration state machine, the durable old-owner fence, the bounded transfer, the crash-safe promotion and the successor's activation are implemented and verified, the DLQ dependency now uses the real Q1 recovery, and the deterministic migration crash matrix executes against real processes. The coordinated source-plus-DLQ handover is not implemented, so C-02 stays IN_PROGRESS.
evidence.observed_result: The Rust suites pass with zero ignored tests (307 workspace tests). The migration campaign passes all seven scenarios. The crash matrix executes seven scenarios against real broker processes and reports PASS for every one; each scenario pauses a broker at a named barrier, kills it with SIGKILL, restarts it on the original storage and checks the invariant of that window. A scenario that never reaches its barrier is a failure and a run with no executed scenario is never a pass.
evidence.fencing_implemented: The durable partition owns the fencing state, not only the routing layer. Partition::set_authority installs Authority {owner, epoch, lease} from committed control-plane metadata; the command is ordered with durable mutations in the actor. Publication, deduplicated retry, consumer FETCH, ACK, NACK and terminal disposition (quarantine and DLQ) all check the authority before starting and fail closed with a stale-epoch error when the local node is not the committed owner. The lease is bounded and counted from local installation, so an expired lease fails closed and a restart never extends it. An older epoch can never replace a newer authority. A mutation whose lease expires during its barrier is reported as an uncertain outcome, never a false COMMITTED_LOCAL. Standalone partitions (no installed authority) keep the previous single-node behaviour.
evidence.fencing_evidence: Actor tests prove: standalone partitions are unfenced; a foreign owner is fenced for publish, fetch, ack and nack; an expired lease fails closed; a newer authority fences the previous owner and an older epoch cannot replace it. Two real broker processes prove: a publication to the non-owner is forwarded once to the owner, the owner performs the durable commit and returns its own offset, the producer token retry returns the same offset without a second record, and an expired ownership lease stops the old owner from committing while its committed history stays readable.
evidence.raft_library_decision: openraft 0.9.26 selected deliberately (the architecture references 0.9.x; 0.10 changes the storage and network contracts). It is pinned exactly with the features serde and storage-v2. The v2 traits are used as published: RaftLogStorage with a LogFlushed completion callback, RaftLogReader, vote and committed-index persistence, RaftStateMachine with a snapshot builder, RaftNetwork (vote, append entries, install snapshot) and RaftNetworkFactory. Library types stay inside the dedicated crates/metadata-raft adapter; the public control-plane model does not depend on OpenRaft internals, and the Raft log index is unrelated to Q1 application offsets.
evidence.remaining_work: Exact next steps: (1) implement the minimal coordinated source-plus-DLQ handover: bind the dependent DLQ partition to the committed migration plan, stage both histories separately, fence both, transfer and verify both final inventories, verify every committed source terminal reference against the transferred DLQ history, commit a bundle activation and promote both histories with their original incarnations. Today the DLQ is required and validated before activation but it is not transferred with the source, so a source whose DLQ lives on another node cannot be handed over; (2) execute the remaining crash windows: during the initial transfer, after a chunk append before its durable sync, after the chunk sync before its acknowledgement, after the finalize before the following transition, during the final post-fence delta, after the first new owner durable commit, a metadata leader crash while a migration transition is pending, and the adversarial transfer cases (missing manifest, corrupt segment, conflicting destination, wrong identity or epoch, conflicting migration id, missing and conflicting chunks); (3) add a directional transport fault so a live but isolated old owner can be tested; the current asymmetric evidence stops the old owner or blocks the successor; (4) execute the DLQ correctness scenarios (duplicate disposition retry, pending terminal at migration start, crash after the DLQ commit before the source terminal closure, interrupted DLQ promotion, source promoted while the DLQ promotion is incomplete).
evidence.limitations: The lease-expiry fallback stays unsupported: a handover needs a durable fence of the actual old owner, and a local timer of the successor never proves a remote owner stopped writing. Activation has a deliberate unavailable interval. The crash matrix covers seven windows, not the whole assignment list. The DLQ is validated but not migrated with the source. The transfer re-sends the final inventory rather than resuming per segment. All processes share one machine, so the evidence proves protocol behaviour and not independent physical failure domains.
evidence.next_note: C-02 stays IN_PROGRESS until the coordinated source-plus-DLQ handover and the remaining crash windows are implemented and executed. C-03 must not start before C-02 is DONE.
evidence.raft_root_cause: The follower assertion was a storage contract violation, not a consensus bug. The file-backed log keyed its records by an internal sequence counter instead of entry.log_id.index, so a range request for index 1 answered with the entry whose log id was 0 and openraft's own check (first entry index == prev_log_id.next_index()) failed. Two further violations had the same shape: the log reader was built from a copy of the index taken when the reader was created, so an entry appended later was reported as missing (openraft requires a non-empty result for a non-empty range), and the state machine returned a result only for normal entries while openraft asserts one result per applied entry. All three are fixed and covered by tests.
evidence.raft_implemented: crates/metadata-raft implements a real three-voter metadata group on openraft 0.9.26. The log storage is a versioned, checksummed file format (MRL1, records of length, CRC32C and payload) keyed by entry.log_id.index; a corrupt, truncated or discontinuous log fails closed on open and is never reset, truncate removes the entry at the given index and everything after it, purge removes everything up to and including it and the purge point is persisted so a restart still reports it. The LogFlushed callback fires only after the data is durable; a failed flush is an uncertain write that poisons the storage and fails closed. The state machine applies committed commands deterministically, keeps ownership epochs monotonic, rejects an unknown owner and persists the applied state atomically after every apply. Snapshots are published durably as an image plus metadata, validated before they are served or installed, and an interrupted publication leaves the previous snapshot intact. The peer protocol is a length-prefixed, CRC32C-checked JSON frame over loopback TCP carrying only the library's own vote, append-entries and snapshot messages; no second consensus algorithm exists. Bootstrap is explicit and refuses to re-initialize existing storage, and a restart recovers the cluster identity, the votes, the log and the applied revisions.
evidence.raft_evidence: In-process: three voters elect a leader through the library, a committed command reaches every voter's state machine, a 1/3 minority cannot commit, a killed leader is replaced in a later term and the new leader keeps the committed metadata, a restarted follower catches up, a follower that returns behind a compacted log is brought current by a snapshot installation, all three nodes restart from their original directories, revisions increase monotonically and an ownership epoch never regresses. Multi-process: scripts/test_metadata_raft.py starts three real metadata processes, observes the election, the majority commit with follower replication, the replacement of a SIGKILLed leader, the refusal of a minority and the recovery of the committed metadata after a restart. These are three processes on one machine, so they prove protocol behaviour and not independent physical failure domains.
evidence.committed_authority: Only committed and applied metadata may become authoritative. The metadata group publishes its applied state as the immutable rovqet_control::MetadataSnapshot, which is installed into the C-01 MetadataStore and turned into the Q1 ownership authority through the existing Partition::set_authority seam; the actor-level fencing checks are unchanged. The store stays empty until the first snapshot is committed, so the data plane fails closed while the group has no committed metadata, an older or equal revision is rejected, and a snapshot of another cluster identity is refused. A static C-01 fixture and Raft mode are mutually exclusive: a broker configured with both refuses to start, so a fixture can never override committed Raft metadata. A Raft election alone never revokes an old owner and never activates a replacement owner; the authority is taken verbatim from the committed snapshot and the lease is counted from local installation.
evidence.migration_implemented: The handover is a committed state machine, a bounded transfer and a durable revocation. BeginMigration binds the migration id, the source and target, the incarnation and both epochs; AdvanceMigration moves it one stage at a time. The state machine rejects a stale expected epoch, a concurrent migration of the same partition, a conflicting migration id, a skipped stage, a fence whose evidence does not match the migration, an activation without fence evidence, an activation without a verified transfer and an activation without target readiness. Only the committed activation moves the placement to the new owner and epoch. The old-owner fence is a record of the Q1 WAL: it is written by the actor that serializes the durable mutations, it is synced before the proof is returned and recovery replays it, so a restarted owner cannot regain its mutation authority. The consumer fetch path checks the revocation before it claims a generation, because claiming a generation writes a durable checkpoint. The transfer declares its inventory, moves bounded digest protected chunks that never carry a path, and verifies the complete inventory before the finalize; a repeated chunk is idempotent, the same identity with different bytes is refused and a missing chunk keeps the finalize from succeeding. The transfer is keyed by an inventory identity, so the history that the fence made final is a second, separately verified inventory. The coordinator drives the stages in order: transfer, verify, fence durably, commit the fence proof, transfer the final delta, commit the activation. A failure at any stage leaves the old owner authoritative.
evidence.migration_evidence: The end-to-end test runs three metadata voters, a Q1 source partition with committed history, and a source and a target broker that talk over real loopback TCP. The metadata group commits the placement and the migration; the source transfers its committed history; the target verifies the inventory; the source fences itself; the fence proof and the verified transfer watermark are committed; the final delta is transferred and verified; the activation is committed and the committed placement moves to the target with the new ownership epoch. The fenced old owner then refuses another publication. The fence tests prove that the proof exists only after the durable boundary, that a fenced owner refuses publication, acknowledgement, rejection and delivery, that a restarted fenced owner still refuses, that a fence without the committed authority or for a stale epoch is refused, that a second fence is refused, and that the committed history survives the fence and can be recovered by a successor.
evidence.activation_implemented: The successor now really opens the transferred WAL as its active Q1 partition. The storage lifecycle is explicit: STAGING -> VERIFIED -> FENCE_CONFIRMED -> ACTIVATION_COMMITTED -> PROMOTED -> ACTIVE. A node without a committed placement stays inactive. A node that the committed metadata names as the owner opens its route; a successor of a committed migration never initializes an empty log as a substitute for the transferred history, it promotes the verified inventory into its partition directory and opens that. The route is a replaceable handle, so a broker goes from inactive target to active owner at runtime and no session keeps a stale mutation authority. The promotion is crash-safe and recoverable: the intent is journalled before the first file moves, every file is published with a digest check, an already published file is verified and skipped, the directory is synced and a durable record states that the promotion completed. A partition directory that holds unrelated or already active storage is refused and the source storage is never touched. The dependent history is checked before the promotion: a migration whose DLQ dependency cannot be shown locally keeps the successor inactive. A follower forwards its proposal to the committed leader instead of pretending that it can commit on its own.
evidence.activation_evidence: The in-process end-to-end test proves the real behaviour: the successor opens the transferred history, the log incarnation is unchanged, a producer retry with the original token returns the original offset without a duplicate publication, the transferred message is delivered at its original offset and the fenced old owner refuses another publication. Five promotion tests cover the publish, the refusal of a target with unrelated storage, the idempotent repeat of a partially published promotion, the refusal of a tampered file and the refusal of an inventory that differs from the verified manifest. Three dependency tests cover a migration without dependencies, a migration whose DLQ dependency is unavailable (the activation is blocked) and a migration whose DLQ destination is independently available.
evidence.dlq_validation_fix: The dependency check accepted any file named MANIFEST, so a corrupt, unrelated or empty destination satisfied it. It now runs the real WAL recovery on the destination: the partition identity, the incarnation, the manifest, the segment inventory, every record checksum and the committed watermark are validated, and the destination must be of the local durable class. The committed terminal references are still verified when the source opens with that destination configured, so the successor stays inactive when a proof is missing. The synthetic fixture that wrote arbitrary bytes is now a negative test and the positive case uses a genuinely committed DLQ publication.
evidence.crash_matrix: Seven deterministic windows are executed: before the durable fence, after it, before the activation commit, after the promotion intent, before the successor route opens, after it opens, and the case where the successor is unreachable while the source keeps serving. Each window is a separate cluster on its own directories and ports; the victim is killed with SIGKILL at a named barrier and restarted on its original storage; the invariant of the window is checked and the verdict is recorded in benchmarks/evidence/c02-crash-matrix/verdicts.json.
evidence.quorum_evidence: A committed migration survives a metadata leader crash: the replacement keeps the migration record at its committed stage. A minority cannot advance the migration and the committed revision does not move, and a restarted voter recovers the committed migration state. The asymmetric-partition test proves that an unreachable old owner blocks the activation: without a durable fence proof the placement keeps the old owner and epoch.
